D.t: Ed Markey leads by 32.7 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 934,134 votes; a one point swing is about 14,297 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +25.6 and D +39.5. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +24.5. Your best recent poll is Suffolk University/Boston Globe at D +26.6; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +23.2. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Middlesex, a projected net 328,577 votes; Suffolk, a projected net 173,845 votes; Norfolk, a projected net 107,342 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Bristol, D +7.0, 7.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Ed Markey runs furthest behind in Worcester, Plymouth, Barnstable. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.
Groups big enough to move the race: Men, 44% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.23 points; Incomes $125K and up, 12% of voters, 60 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 0.60 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Ed Markey: Immigration voters 28 to 69, Men 58 to 39, Incomes $125K and up 60 to 38. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.3M cash against $712K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $205K helping John Deaton and $43K helping Ed Markey.
